The stock market is a complex and ever-changing system. There are many ways to analyze financial data in order to make investment decisions, and each method has its own strengths and weaknesses. The five most common technical analysis methods are: Moving Averages, Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), Fibonacci Retracement, Bollinger Bands, and Relative Strength Index (RSI). Moving Averages smooths out price data by creating a constantly updated average price. MACD is a trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between two moving averages. Fibonacci Retracement is a technical analysis tool that identifies potential support and resistance levels based on historical price movements. Bollinger Bands are a volatility indicator that shows the range of price movement relative to a moving average. RSI is a momentum indicator that measures the speed and change of price movements.
